evidence_requirement: Probe 1: run the identical probe payload in every substrate and record the four outcomes per substrate as a matrix. Probe 2 (mechanically different): read the router's selection logic and identify which substrate untrusted/third-party code is actually routed to, then check that cell of the matrix - a strong sandbox that untrusted code is never routed to provides zero protection.
inputs: the substrate router and its selection rules
a probe payload that attempts, in each substrate: read a credential path, list sibling processes, write outside its root, and open an outbound socket
orchestration-patterns skill: Windows has no native OS-level process sandbox
question_or_target: For each substrate the program will route work to (local process, worktree, WSL2, docker, cloud sandbox), what does the boundary actually prevent - filesystem reach, network egress, credential visibility, process visibility - and where does the router send untrusted code?
tests_required: the probe must SUCCEED at all four actions in the deliberately unisolated local case, proving the probe can detect capability at all before any 'blocked' result is believed
title: Isolation review of the execution-substrate ladder
